statusMeaning: Expected behaviors for a future implementation. Structural checks on this file are not behavioral tests or evidence of readiness.

cases.title: Unknown availability
cases.given: A retrospective row has effective_at but source_first_observed_at=null.
cases.when: Build a historical training set.
cases.assertion: Do not copy event_at or bulk ingested_at into source_first_observed_at.

cases.title: Late correction isolation
cases.given: Revision A was observed before cutoff; revision B corrects it after cutoff.
cases.when: Reconstruct as-known data and mutate revision B.
cases.assertion: Earlier training data, settings and predictions remain unchanged.

cases.title: Completion is scoped
cases.given: An extract date is current but the relevant population/period has completion_status=unknown.
cases.when: Score or publish that period as complete.
cases.assertion: Max event date and calendar closure cannot establish completeness.

cases.title: Boundary and duplicate identity
cases.given: Two revisions conflict at the same identity/version, or an outcome arrives one millisecond after cutoff.
cases.when: Select one revision per record at an inclusive cutoff.
cases.assertion: Exactly-at-cutoff availability is eligible; duplicates are not arbitrarily selected.

cases.title: Missing versus zero
cases.given: Two closed-looking months contain null count/unknown completion and zero count/verified completion respectively.
cases.when: Construct the monthly series.
cases.assertion: Never coalesce absence to zero or interpolate a target.

cases.title: Exposure mismatch
cases.given: Voluntary exits cover population A; the supplied denominator covers population B or only month-end stock.
cases.when: Compute a rate forecast.
cases.assertion: Counts may remain separately eligible; future exposure is not inferred.

cases.title: Classification revision
cases.given: A separation was initially involuntary and later corrected to voluntary.
cases.when: Backtest at a cutoff before the correction.
cases.assertion: Current final counts must not rewrite the older training vintage.

cases.title: Estimand identity
cases.given: The source metric is mean respondent favorable-answer share.
cases.when: Label it percent of satisfied employees or derive unfavorable=100-favorable.
cases.assertion: Neutral share, item rules and employee-level classification are not inferred.

cases.title: Nonresponse and denominator
cases.given: A wave has 100 eligible people, 60 respondents and variable answered-item counts.
cases.when: Compute participation and a respondent-share measure.
cases.assertion: Participation uses eligible people; respondent-share mean uses valid respondents under the scoring specification.

cases.title: Missing score preservation
cases.given: The metric is null because scoring rules are unverified or the cell is suppressed.
cases.when: Serialize it or fit a wave model.
cases.assertion: Null must never become numeric zero.

cases.title: Instrument and population break
cases.given: Two waves have changed items/scales or eligibility with no verified bridge.
cases.when: Pool them or interpolate monthly observations.
cases.assertion: Retain separate versions and report insufficient comparable waves.

cases.title: Suppression and cross-query reconstruction
cases.given: A proposed group is below the approved minimum or can be reconstructed by subtracting released totals.
cases.when: Prepare aggregate outputs.
cases.assertion: A minimum cell count alone does not make related totals or overlapping queries releasable.

cases.title: Synthetic eNPS isolation
cases.given: Independent arbitrary eNPS responses are presented as a new wave of employee satisfaction.
cases.when: Attach them to a goal or historical trend.
cases.assertion: The held eNPS source and its disabled gate remain outside this proposal.

cases.title: Open search is censored
cases.given: A requisition has no observed actual start and is open/cancelled or status is unknown.
cases.when: Construct lead-time labels and cohort accounting.
cases.assertion: Do not create zero duration or substitute a planned/hire date; retain denominator dispositions.

cases.title: Stage availability
cases.given: An opening exists at cutoff; accepted offer/actual start and final pipeline counts occur later.
cases.when: Fit an opening-time model.
cases.assertion: Calendar features may be known; final pipeline counts and revised target dates are not opening-known.

cases.title: Decision/start/capacity separation
cases.given: hire_date matches accepted response while actual start is later; capacity-ready time is absent.
cases.when: Produce expected hiring and capacity outcomes.
cases.assertion: No start-date substitution and no inferred productive-capacity date.

cases.title: Trend without comparison
cases.given: Training completion and an improving outcome trend exist, but no assignment/comparison design.
cases.when: Estimate program effect.
cases.assertion: Permit explicitly labeled descriptive change or user-assumed scenario only.

cases.title: Post-outcome assignment
cases.given: Treatment groups were chosen using later outcomes or post-treatment variables.
cases.when: Define an effect contrast.
cases.assertion: Assignment, eligibility and adjustment inputs must respect the target design and timing.

cases.title: Nonadherence and attrition
cases.given: Assigned intervention units include nonparticipants; follow-up/nonresponse differs between arms.
cases.when: Calculate an effect under the registered assignment contrast.
cases.assertion: Do not silently drop nonparticipants or treat nonresponders as satisfied.

cases.title: Confounded comparison
cases.given: Intervention and comparison groups differ in pre-intervention trends, overlap or concurrent changes.
cases.when: Apply an observational contrast.
cases.assertion: A descriptive difference or passing trend test alone is not causal identification.

cases.title: Independent units and overlapping benefits
cases.given: Repeated rows come from very few assigned groups; two interventions affect the same population/window.
cases.when: Compute uncertainty and combine benefits.
cases.assertion: Use assignment-unit dependence; do not count repeated rows as independent groups or sum overlapping effects.

cases.title: Fabricated historical availability
cases.given: A generator creates observed_at values for an existing bulk-loaded company extract.
cases.when: Label the result as verified company history.
cases.assertion: Only separate constructed-synthetic records may carry simulated observation times.

cases.title: Frozen final assessment
cases.given: Future synthetic outcomes or generator-only true effects are modified after a development fit.
cases.when: Repeat development and selection.
cases.assertion: Outcome-based generated predictions, final-block tuning and ground-truth sidecar access fail.

cases.title: Realistic failure scenarios
cases.given: Pinned generator cases include zero/adverse/delayed effects, censoring, nonresponse and source revisions.
cases.when: Validate the generator and demonstration report.
cases.assertion: No guaranteed improvement; valid stage order, bounded scores, nonnegative counts/exposure and reproducibility must hold.

cases.title: Insufficient calibration
cases.given: A few overlapping folds or correlated groups are available and model disagreement exists.
cases.when: Construct a prediction/effect confidence range.
cases.assertion: Prediction uncertainty and causal-effect uncertainty require separate method and coverage/design evidence.
